text:
kevin: noticed a perf regression on int8 path after the batching heuristic tweak earlier today. tail latency up ~30% on p95 for small prompt workloads. attaching traces.

maya: thanks, can you drop the perfetto/trace link and nsys summary?

kevin: perfetto: https://perfetto.local/trace/abcd1234 (private)
kevin: nsys summary: 
```
==NVPROF== Kernel Summary:
conv_int8_kernel  64.2ms (hot path)
deq_pack         12.1ms (host->gpu copy spikes visible)
kv_read          8.4ms (lots of small reads)
```

dmitri: interesting that conv_int8_kernel is dominant. was that kernel selected by the new kernel selector?

kevin: yes, selector chose int8_conv_fused_v2 for most sequences. before the change we were using int8_conv_fused_v1 which had lower per-kernel launch overhead for short sequences.

alex: can you paste the exact command you used to generate the nsys profile? quick sanity check: sampling vs full trace matters.

kevin: ran `nsys profile --output=run1 --sample=cpu --trace=cupti --duration=60 --target-processes=all ./serve_bench --batch-size=auto`
kevin: also attached a small perfetto slice showing batch start/stop markers.

natalie: the KV cache behavior looks suspicious in the trace: I see frequent cache evictions aligned with batch boundaries. Might be our cache padding heuristic causing extra host->device syncs.

dmitri: that would explain the hostcopy spikes (deq_pack). If batches are forced to re-prime KV for each request instead of doing incremental updates, we pay the copy cost repeatedly.

maya: two hypotheses: (1) selector's kernel tiling increases kernel concurrency but also increases memory working set leading to more KV evictions; (2) batching heuristic now groups requests by size incorrectly, producing many tiny batches that trigger dequant/pack repeatedly.

kevin: I dumped batching debug flags: `BATCHER_MAX_WAIT_MS=5 BATCHER_MIN_SIZE=1 BATCH_BY_TOKEN=true` — suspect BATCH_BY_TOKEN and min wait shrink caused oscillation.

alex: can we repro with a focused microbench? recommend: run `./bencher --workload=short_prompts --threads=8 --batcher=prod` and capture `nsys` with kernel timeline + host memcpy events. keep run short (30s) and attach perfetto for timeline.

kevin: ran that, attaching quick logs: 
```
[bench] requests=1200 rps=40 p95=220ms p50=60ms
[trace] memcpy_htod  spikes at t=12.3s,13.1s,14.0s
[kernel] int8_conv_fused_v2 launches 600 times, avg 110us launch overhead
```

natalie: avg 110us launch overhead * 600 = 66ms extra per second-ish depending on parallelism. not trivial.

dmitri: action items I propose:
- add a KV warm/retain option to avoid evicting between tiny batches (`KV_RETAIN_ON_BATCH_SPLIT=true`)
- add a short-circuit in kernel selector to prefer lower-launch-overhead kernel for seq_len < 64 (`prefer_low_launch=true if seq<64`)
- instrument batcher to emit metrics: batch_count, avg_batch_size, kv_evictions_per_minute

kevin: implemented the selector short-circuit locally, re-ran microbench: p95 dropped from 220ms -> 170ms, memcpy spikes reduced by ~40%.

maya: nice. any accuracy differences with the alternate kernel? int8 quantization should be identical, but fused micro-ops sometimes reorder ops; need to run a quick eval set.

kevin: ran eval on 200 samples, no diff in top-1 generation. FP8 path still not impacted by this selector change.

alex: also check dequant CPU path. I saw the worker thread doing dequant->reformat on CPU before memcpy. maybe we can overlap dequant with memcpy by moving reformat onto GPU if possible.

natalie: that would reduce host-side wall time. but moving reformat to GPU requires supporting a different tensor layout; kernel changes needed.

dmitri: short term: overlap by using an async worker pool and prefetch buffers. medium term: upstream kernel change.

kevin: quick patch: `KV_RETAIN_ON_BATCH_SPLIT=true` + selector short-circuit + worker pool yielded p95 150ms on the bench. CPU utilization spread improved.

perf-bot: scheduled nightly perf job with the new flags enabled for canary cluster. job id: perf-1957-canary-01

maya: awesome. next steps: (1) run full regression eval on 2k prompts, (2) add batcher metrics to console, (3) consider adding a kernel scoring metric that includes launch-overhead for small sequences.

kevin: I'll open a PR with the selector flag and metrics. tagging @dmitri @natalie for review. thanks all :mag_right: :thumbsup:
